title: Mitsubishi Motors Cuts Profit Outlook on Middle East Conflict and Bets on New Pajero
dek: Mitsubishi now expects operating profit to fall 7.3% this fiscal year, citing weaker sales, higher costs and a limited hybrid lineup as fuel prices rise.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Rear view of a black 1982 Mitsubishi Pajero SUV

keyPoints: Mitsubishi Motors cut its full-year profit forecast on Nov. 6, saying the Middle East conflict is undercutting sales and raising costs.
Operating profit is now expected to fall to ¥70 billion ($444.8 million) in the fiscal year ending March 31, from ¥75.5 billion a year earlier, a 7.3% decline.
In August the company had predicted operating profit would grow 19% to ¥90 billion.
Higher fuel prices are lifting demand for electrified vehicles in markets such as Southeast Asia, where Mitsubishi has a limited hybrid range.
body:
Mitsubishi Motors has lowered its profit outlook for the current fiscal year, citing weaker sales and higher costs tied to the conflict in the Middle East.

## The revised numbers

According to Automotive News, the Japanese carmaker now expects operating profit to decline 7.3% rather than grow. It projects operating profit of ¥70 billion ($444.8 million) for the year ending March 31, down from ¥75.5 billion ($479.8 million) the year before. In August, the company had forecast profit rising 19% to ¥90 billion ($571.9 million). It also cut its net income outlook to roughly flat with the prior year, after earlier expecting net income to more than double.

The change matters because it reverses the direction of the company's guidance, not just its size. A forecast for growth has become a forecast for decline within a few months, which tells investors the company's earlier assumptions about volume and cost no longer hold.

## Why it happened

President Keisuke Kishiura attributed the cut to sluggish sales and rising costs, partly due to the Middle East conflict, Automotive News reported. Shipping disruptions and high oil prices have hit several automakers this year, and Mitsubishi is more exposed than most because its electrified lineup is limited.

The war has also pushed buyers toward electrified vehicles in some markets. Automotive News reported that higher fuel prices have fanned demand for hybrids and other electrified models in Southeast Asia, where Mitsubishi has only a narrow hybrid range. Demand is moving in a direction the company is not yet well equipped to serve.

## The Pajero plan

The company is pinning its recovery on a new Pajero, and on a planned pickup truck, according to coverage of the results. The sources reviewed did not provide sales targets, pricing or launch dates for either model, so the size of any rebound remains unclear. Investors will want to see how quickly the new SUV reaches showrooms and whether it can carry margins that the current lineup is not delivering.

## What to watch

The next checkpoints are the company's quarterly updates and any early sales figures for the new Pajero. Investors will also be watching whether the Middle East conflict keeps fuel prices high enough to shift demand further toward hybrids, and whether Mitsubishi can add electrified options quickly enough to capture that shift.

marketImpact.summary: Mitsubishi is a smaller, mostly internal-combustion player with a limited hybrid range. A forecast cut for profit and net income signals weaker volume and margins, which is a negative read for the company's near-term earnings path. The effect on the wider auto sector is limited.
marketImpact.timeframe: Next 1-3 months, until the next quarterly update and first Pajero sales data
